$comment: Metafield and metaobject definitions for an apparel storefront.
Field names mirror src/data/schema.ts so code and admin stay in sync.
Types are Shopify metafield type identifiers, verified against
shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/metafields/list-of-data-types.
Apply these once per store, before any product data is entered.
Order matters: metaobject definitions must exist before the
metaobject_reference metafield that points at them.
Set this per product FIRST. It is what unlocks the predefined
category metafields below. Without a category you get none of them.

examples.tee: Apparel & Accessories > Clothing > Clothing Tops > T-Shirts
examples.shirt: Apparel & Accessories > Clothing > Clothing Tops > Shirts
examples.knitwear: Apparel & Accessories > Clothing > Clothing Tops > Sweaters

$comment: Colour and size are VARIANT OPTIONS, not product metafields.
Connect each option to its category metafield entries rather than
typing free text. Doing so gives three things you cannot get from
plain text options: colour swatches on the storefront, renaming in
one place that propagates everywhere, and standardised values for
Google/Meta channels.
Modelling colour as an option is also what makes variant grouping
automatic — one product IS one style. Only stores that already have
one product per colourway need the style_code field below.
PREDEFINED by Shopify's Standard Product Taxonomy. Do not recreate
these as custom metafields — you would lose the default entry lists,
channel mapping, and filter support. Populate the ones listed.
Availability varies slightly by category (trousers have no neckline).

customProductMetafields.name: Model height
customProductMetafields.description: Height of the model in the product photography.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Record this at the shoot. It cannot be recovered later without reshooting, and it is the single highest-value line on the page.

customProductMetafields.name: Model size worn
customProductMetafields.description: The size the model is actually wearing in the photos.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Must match a real size on this product. Pairs with model_height — one without the other is not usable.

customProductMetafields.name: Runs true to size
customProductMetafields.description: Whether the garment runs small, true, or large.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Set from review data once you have it, from fit sessions before then. Publishing 'runs large' prevents returns — it does not lose sales.

customProductMetafields.name: Fabric weight (gsm)
customProductMetafields.description: Fabric weight in grams per square metre.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: From the mill spec sheet. Shoppers use it to judge opacity and season.

customProductMetafields.name: Cut
customProductMetafields.description: How close the garment is cut.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Keep to these four values. Inventing per-style names ("easy", "boxy") makes the filter useless.

customProductMetafields.name: Care instructions
customProductMetafields.clientNote: One instruction per entry, not a paragraph. Entries render as a list.

customProductMetafields.name: Product details
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Only specific, checkable facts. Vague sustainability language erodes trust rather than building it.

customProductMetafields.name: Short summary
customProductMetafields.description: One-line description for cards and search results.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Say what the garment is and its most distinctive property. Not marketing copy.

customProductMetafields.name: Size chart
customProductMetafields.description: Which size chart applies to this product.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: Reference a shared chart — do not duplicate per product. One edit then updates every product using it.

customProductMetafields.name: Style code
customProductMetafields.description: Style-level identifier, distinct from variant SKU.
customProductMetafields.clientNote: ONLY needed if your existing data has one product per colourway. If colour is a variant option, the product already IS the style and this is redundant.

metaobjectDefinitions.name: Size chart
metaobjectDefinitions.$comment: Authored once, referenced by many products.

fields.clientNote: State which. Conflating garment and body measurements is itself a return driver.
A chart without instructions is guesswork. Say where to put the tape.

$comment: Things people wrongly model as metafields. Keep them where they belong.
notMetafields.inventory: Variant inventory quantity. Native field. Stock-aware size filters depend on this being accurate per size, in real time.
notMetafields.price: Variant price and compare-at price. Native fields.
notMetafields.images: Product media, assigned per colourway variant. Native.
notMetafields.reviews: A reviews platform (e.g. Okendo) owns reviewer height, size purchased and true-to-size. Do NOT build this as metafields — you would also be building collection, moderation, and request timing.
notMetafields.returnsPolicy: Store-level content, not per product. Render from a shared snippet so it cannot drift between pages.
